title: dep-scan finding
description: One result reported by dep-scan. Every category dep-scan writes, from classic vulnerabilities through memory-safety defects, binary hardening and license issues, uses this one shape. The id field carries the line-free fingerprint (dsf1) that baselines and suppressions key on; locations and evidence carry the reasons; coverage says whether the analysis that owns the finding actually ran. Extensions go in the properties array, which is why the objects stay closed.

id.description: The finding fingerprint: dsf1 followed by the SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical payload described in analysis_lib.findings.fingerprint. The id never contains line or column numbers, so baselines and suppressions survive unrelated edits. A future change to the algorithm would produce dsf2 ids and never alter a dsf1 id.

category.description: The kind of result. vulnerability covers advisory-backed findings; the other categories come from analyzers, binary analysis, code review and project health checks.

rule.description: The advisory id or the analyzer rule id that fired, for example CVE-2021-23337, GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw or RUSI-MS-PANIC-001. Advisory ids keep their canonical case; other rule ids are kept as given.

title.description: A short human-readable statement of the finding. Titles never copy source text, argument values or environment values.

severity.description: The severity the producer assigned to this finding.

confidence.description: How sure the producer is that the finding is real. Absent when the producer does not express confidence.

cwes.description: The CWE numbers that classify the defect, for example 77 for command injection or 476 for a null pointer dereference.

components.description: The affected components as package URLs. Versions are allowed here; the fingerprint that the id is built from strips them.

items.description: One place the finding applies to.

locations.description: Where the finding lives. Findings without a source location, such as a vulnerable package or a binary hardening gap, point at the manifest, lockfile or binary that declares the affected component.

evidence.description: Ids of the records in the scan's evidence file that back this finding. The evidence schema is published separately.

coverage.description: Whether the analysis that owns this finding ran, and why not when it did not.

exploitability.description: The exploitability assessment across the five axes, filled by the exploitability grading rules.

triage.description: The human decision about this finding, using the CycloneDX 1.7 impact analysis vocabulary.

fix.description: How to move past the finding, when the producer knows a way.

producer.description: The tool that produced this finding.

items.description: One link a reader of the finding may follow.

references.description: Links to advisories, upstream reports or documentation for this finding.

properties.description: Producer-specific extensions, carried as name and value pairs the way CycloneDX does. Keeping extensions here lets the rest of the object stay closed.

location.description: One place a finding applies to: a source position, a function, or a binary file and offset. Every field is optional because binary and manifest findings carry a different subset than source findings do.

file.description: Path relative to the scan root with forward slashes. For findings without source code, the manifest or lockfile that declared the component.

line.description: Line number in file, counting from 1.

column.description: Column number on the line, counting from 1.

end_line.description: Last line of the range, when the finding spans lines.

end_column.description: Last column of the range, when the finding spans columns.

function.description: Name of the enclosing function, when the producer resolved one.

binary.description: Name of the binary the finding applies to, for example usr/bin/hello.

offset.description: Offset inside the binary, counting from 0.

coverage.description: Whether the relevant analysis ran. A state of not_assessed means the analyzer did not run, failed, hit a budget or lacked data; it is a different state from assessed and nothing found, and a policy gate or VEX statement must never treat one as the other.

state.description: assessed when the analysis that owns this finding ran to completion; not_assessed when it did not.

items.description: One reason the capability did not assess what it was asked to.

reasons.description: Why coverage stopped. Required, with at least one entry, whenever state is not_assessed.

coverage-reason.description: One concrete reason a capability did not assess what it was asked to.

capability.description: The capability that could not run, named the way depscan doctor names them, for example memory-safety:c or reachability:dotnet.

reason.description: Short machine-readable reason the capability did not run, for example tool-missing, budget-exceeded, data-missing or data-stale.

detail.description: Human-readable detail, for example the tool version that was found or the path of the stale shard.

exploitability.description: The exploitability assessment. The five axes say how confident the analysis is about each property of the finding, and the grade summarises them.

grade.description: The overall exploitability grade derived from the axes.

rule.description: The grading rule or policy that produced the grade, so a reader can see why the axes map to it.

items.description: One axis that could not be assessed.

unassessed.description: The axes that could not be assessed for this finding.

witness.description: Id of the evidence record that decided the grade.

exploitability-axes.description: The five exploitability axes, each graded on the same scale.

presence.description: Whether the defect the finding describes is present in the assessed code.

reach.description: Whether the defect is reachable from code or interfaces an attacker controls.

exposure.description: Whether the component or code carrying the defect is exposed where it runs.

barrier.description: Whether a mitigation stands between the attacker and the defect. proven or likely means a barrier exists; unlikely or refuted means none does.

pressure.description: Whether attackers have motive or precedent for exploiting this defect, for example public exploit availability.

triage.description: The human decision about the finding. The state, justification and response values are copied from the CycloneDX 1.7 schema bundled in analysis_lib.data.cyclonedx.

state.description: The impact analysis state, from the CycloneDX 1.7 impactAnalysisState enum.

justification.description: The impact analysis justification, from the CycloneDX 1.7 impactAnalysisJustification enum. CycloneDX recommends a justification for every not_affected state.

items.description: One response to the finding, from the CycloneDX 1.7 response enum.

responses.description: The responses chosen for this finding.

detail.description: Free-form detail about the triage decision, including why the component is not affected.

expires.description: When the triage decision expires and the finding returns to triage, as an RFC 3339 date-time.

fix.description: How to move past the finding.

fixed_versions.description: Versions of the affected component that resolve the finding.

upgrade_path.description: Ordered steps or intermediate versions that take the project from its current state to the fix, when a single bump is not possible.

recommendation.description: The recommended action, in one human-readable sentence.

producer.description: The analyzer that produced the finding. The version lets results be traced to a release.

name.description: Producer name, for example dep-scan, rusi or blint.

version.description: Version of the producer that wrote the finding.

reference.description: One link a reader of the finding may follow.

type.description: What the link is, for example advisory, documentation or upstream-issue.

finding-property.description: One extension property, carried as a name and value pair the way CycloneDX does.

name.description: Property name. Producers namespace theirs, for example depscan:priority.
